# Station History
[italic]A short history of Corsat Station for new arrivals, as far as the Herald is allowed to tell it.[/italic]
## What We Can Say Corsat Station is a Weyland-Yutani research and prison station on the outer arm of Herculis, out in the Neroid Sector. What the research is for is classified. The United Americas press is barred from reporting on it, and every contract signed here carries a non-disclosure clause longer than the pay schedule. This paper exists in the space those clauses leave open.
## The Domes The Company built Corsat as four sealed biodomes, each behind its own airlocks and ID checkpoints and run from its own control module. - [bold]Gamma[/bold] holds the main landing bay, the administration center, the medbay and most of the housing. - [bold]Sigma[/bold] has the second landing bay, the robotics and data laboratories and a firing range out under the dome, at the far end of the monorail. - [bold]Theta[/bold] grows the station's food in its east and west hydroponics wings. Its terraria keep a jungle, a mesa and a snowfield side by side, and their keepers talk about weather nobody else here has seen. - [bold]Omega[/bold] sits behind its own checkpoint, with its own landing bay for Company flights. Staff do not discuss it and the Herald has never been let past the door.
## The Cell Block Corsat also holds prisoners on Company contract, in the cells off the Gamma security hub. Some are colonial convicts working off their sentences. Some arrived with no paperwork the Herald can find. The Warden answers to the Company, not to any colonial court. We keep asking for the names on the roll. We have not yet been given them.
## The People - Contract scientists rotate in for a season, live in the researcher quarters and leave with their notes sealed. - Engineers, cooks, guards and custodians stay for years and raise families here. - Their children go to the [bold]CORSAT Academy[/bold], read in the station library and learn early which doors not to ask about.
## The Press The Herald started as a bulletin pinned up in the Gamma canteen: shift changes, monorail delays, the names of the people who were hurt. It is still mostly that. On a station where so much is sealed, the ordinary record is worth keeping.
